name: Hadron-Elektron-Ring-Anlage
notes: Injector chain (Klein & Yoshida 2008, Table 1): protons, RFQ - LINAC III (50 MeV) - DESY III (8 GeV) - PETRA (40 GeV) - HERA (920 GeV); electrons and positrons, LINAC II (450 MeV) - PIA - DESY II (7 GeV) - PETRA (12 GeV) - HERA (27.5 GeV). Only HERA has an Atlas record; the pre-accelerators and PETRA are not linked.

Operation dates: DESY's page says "Research operation: 1992-2007" and Klein & Yoshida say "The first HERA data were taken in summer 1992. It ceased operations in June 2007"; the day (30 June 2007) is from Wikipedia and stays on the interval with its low confidence.

beam_energy.note: Replaces the earlier Wikipedia and lecture-notes sourcing. Table 1 of the same paper gives the lepton ring energy as 27.5 GeV.
beam_energy.quote: The energy of the electron (positron) beam was about 27.5 GeV.

circumference.note: DESY's own figure (the same page says "a 6.3-kilometer-long tunnel"). Klein & Yoshida (arXiv:0805.3334), Table 1 caption, write "The main ring is 6223 m in circumference", which differs by 1.8 %; the DESY figure is used and agrees with the tunnel geometry check on the DESY map.

cms_energy.quote: From 1992 to 2007, HERA, the first electron-proton collider, operated at cms energies of about 320 GeV

injection_energy.display: 40 GeV (protons from PETRA); 12 GeV (electrons from PETRA)
injection_energy.note: Table 1, "Chain of (pre)accelerators at HERA and their energies": protons source, RFQ (750 keV), LINAC III (50 MeV), DESY III (8 GeV), PETRA (40 GeV), HERA (920 GeV); electrons source (150 keV), LINAC II (450 MeV), PIA (450 MeV), DESY II (7 GeV), PETRA (12 GeV), HERA (27.5 GeV). PETRA belongs to the colliders stream and has no record on this branch.
injection_energy.quote: Protons Source RFQ LINAC III DESY III PETRA HERA Ep 20 keV 750 keV 50 MeV 8 GeV 40 GeV 920 GeV Electrons Ee Source 150 keV LINAC II 450 MeV PIA 450 MeV DESY II 7 GeV PETRA 12 GeV HERA 27.5 GeV

proton_energy.note: 820 GeV until 1998, 920 GeV from 1998; in the last three months of operation lower proton energies (460 and 575 GeV) were used (same paper).
proton_energy.quote: The energy of the proton beam was initially set to 820 GeV until it was increased to 920 GeV, in 1998, and kept at that value.
